CVE-2026-110816.title: qs.stringify with arrayFormat comma throws TypeError on array elements that cannot be coerced to a string
CVE-2026-110816.description:
### Summary

`qs.stringify` with `arrayFormat: 'comma'` throws `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` when an array element cannot be coerced to a string, such as an object with an own non-callable `toString` (`{ "toString": "x" }`) or a null-prototype object. The comma format joins array elements with `Array.prototype.join` and, under `encodeValuesOnly`, first passes each element through `String()` in `utils.encode`; neither guards against an element whose string coercion fails.

### Details

In `lib/stringify.js`, the comma branch collapses the array with `obj.join(',')`. For an element whose own `toString` is not callable, `ToPrimitive` skips it, falls through to `Object.prototype.valueOf` (which returns the object itself), and throws. Under `encodeValuesOnly: true`, the same element first reaches `String(str)` in `utils.encode` (`lib/utils.js`) and throws there. CVE-2026-119284.title: joserfc: Compact JWS size guard allocates attacker-controlled segments before rejection
CVE-2026-119284.description: joserfc is a Python library that provides an implementation of several JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) standards. Prior to 1.7.6, joserfc compact JWS deserialization calls bytes.split() before enforcing the existing aggregate segment-size limits. When attacker-controlled compact serialization bytes reach deserialize_compact(), the split creates copies of the header, payload, and signature segments before ExceededSizeError rejects them, causing an additional allocation approximately proportional to the supplied token. Requests that exhaust available process memory can therefore cause an availability failure even though signature verification fails. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.6.

bcmgenet_netif_stop() and the Wake-on-LAN branch of bcmgenet_suspend()
both disable the Tx queues first and stop Tx NAPI several steps later. A
completion in flight calls netif_tx_wake_queue() in between, and nothing
stops the queue again, so a transmit can reach the rings after they have
been freed.

Close is safe because dev_deactivate_many() stops the qdisc first.
bcmgenet_suspend() does not, so stop Tx NAPI before the queues on both
paths.

KASAN on a Raspberry Pi CM4, driven from an MTU change because suspend
freezes user space before the callback runs:

BUG: KASAN: use-after-free in bcmgenet_xmit+0x17f8/0x2258
Write of size 8 at addr ffffff8055844a68 by task ksoftirqd/0/14
bcmgenet_xmit+0x17f8/0x2258
dev_hard_start_xmit+0x13c/0x588
sch_direct_xmit+0x108/0x340
__dev_queue_xmit+0x1190/0x3848

CVE-2026-98879.title: isofs: handle set_blocksize failures
CVE-2026-98879.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

isofs: handle set_blocksize failures

isofs uses buffer_heads, which don't handle block size > PAGE_SIZE well.
Without this, mounting we will hit the

BUG_ON(offset >= folio_size(folio));

in folio_set_bh on the first __bread_gfp call.

CVE-2026-99241.title: ntfs: take invalidate_lock in ntfs_filemap_page_mkwrite()
CVE-2026-99241.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ntfs: take invalidate_lock in ntfs_filemap_page_mkwrite()

ntfs_filemap_page_mkwrite() calls iomap_page_mkwrite() without holding
mapping->invalidate_lock, so a concurrent truncate or fallocate can be
in the middle of invalidating pagecache and rewriting the runlist while
the write fault maps blocks and dirties the folio. This races with
ntfs_attr_fallocate(), which merges clusters into the in-memory
runlist, drops the runlist lock, and only afterwards zeroes the newly
allocated clusters on disk; and with the punch-hole/insert/collapse
paths that free clusters after truncating the cache.

Per Documentation/filesystems/locking.rst, ->page_mkwrite() must ensure
there are no truncate/invalidate races, "usually mapping->invalidate_lock
is suitable for proper serialization". xfs takes its mmaplock (= the
invalidate_lock rwsem) shared in exactly this path.
